items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: The drummer was Von Gammon at the time I went there... And Harry Shields... I wouldn't play the melodies. He said, Just play the chords... Harry Shields had a wonderful ear... Harry would say, No, no, that's the wrong change.

ctx.x: Can you just mention a few of the names?

Oh, yes. I remember, for sure, they had... Broken Dishes. Von Gammon. Oh, well, he's talking about my girlfriend now. Broken... I'm just kidding. She could have been. Broken Dishes, who really used to be a real tough girl. She used to beat up all the other girls, you know. She was tattooed. She was tattooed from head to foot. You know, the girls were working on tickets, you know. They'd try to beat one another out of dances, and she'd go back in, and she'd have it out with them. But it was all really part of the…

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: I met Harry Shields, he was playing there at the time... I believe we had just Harry Shields on the clarinet... Harry Shields was sitting right alongside of me... he taught me the right chords, showed me what I should play.

ctx.x: Back to the piano players, are there any others that you remember in that era that were outstanding?

Well, I would say that after I began playing around the suburban movie houses in town, I used to play for silent movies in those days. Played with three pieces. We used to get a dollar a piece a night. We didn't even get our call fair, but I was playing with a violin player by the name of Grasshoff and a drummer, Surpass I believe was his name. We used to go down to the St. Maurice Avenue Theater and play for these silent movies. The silent movies got a bad deal in those days because we were playing Tiger Rag or…
Would he sit down at the piano?

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: I don't remember knowing Steve... Probably I did hear Steve playing... never did get to know who they really was.

ctx.x: I don't remember knowing Steve. He must have been just a little bit before my time, I believe. Well, Harry, Sujohn remembers him well from Victor's.

Well, Harry should, because I'm the same age as Harry. And I should remember Steve, too. Maybe I heard him playing. Like I say, you know, when you're a young kid coming up, you get around, and in those days, it was just a little bit different. I mean, you'd hear a guy and you wouldn't even know who he was. I mean, you'd just know, well, he played good. And probably I did hear Steve playing, because I heard quite a number of fine guys playing piano, and never did get to know who they really was.
